Author: Rajeev Misra

Case :- Criminal Revision No. - 985 of 2002
Revisionist :- Sagiruddin

Opposite Party :- State Of U.P.
Counsel for Revisionist :- Avanish Mishra,Santosh Kumar Upadhyay,Vinod Kumar Upadhyay
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate Hon'ble Rajeev Misra,J.
Heard Mr. V.K. Upadhyay, learned counsel for revisionist and the learned A.G.A. for the State.

This criminal revision has been filed challenging order dated 13.2.2002 passed by Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 2, Allahabad in Criminal Case No. 1673 of 1994 (State Vs.
Sagiruddin), under sections 7(iii)/16(1)(a)(ii) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, P.S. Phoolpur,
District Allahabad, whereby the revisionist has been convicted and accordingly sentenced three months imprisionment along with fine of Rs. 500/- for offence punishable under section 7(iii)/16(1)(ii) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

sentences.text: It transpires from record that revisionist was selling food articles in his shop as General Merchant.

The shop of the revisionist was inspected by Chief Food Inspector on 9.2.1993 at 10 a.m. As according to Food Inspector, the revisionist was not having any licence in respect of food items sold by him, a complaint was filed in Court of Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 2,
Allahabad.

Allahabad

sentences.text:
Sanction was accorded by the Chief Medical Officer, Allahabad to launch prosecution Sagiruddin vs State Of U.P. on 18 October, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50479499/
1 against revisionist for an offence punishable under section 7 (3) and section 16 (1) (a) (ii) of Food Adulteration Act.
The trail commenced and P.W. 1 Sri Sad Guru Saran, retired Food Inspector and P.W. 2 were examined.

The accused was examined under section 313 Cr. P. C. and only three questions were put to the accused, which are quoted here under:-

Ultimately, Court below convicted the accused, vide judgement and order dated 13.2.2002, which order was challenged in appeal and was dismissed by order order dated 8.7.2002.

Learned counsel for the revisionist contends that in the present case,
all the incriminating material and adverse circumstances were not disclosed to the accused under section 313 Cr. P. C.
On this account, trial stands vitiated.

It is then submitted that the accused has been convicted under Sections 7 (3) and 16 (1) (a) (ii)
of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.
There is no finding to that extent recorded by the Trial Court or by the Appellate Court.

He then submits that conviction of revisionist under Section 16 (1) (a) (ii) of Sagiruddin vs State Of U.P. on 18 October, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/50479499/
2 Food Adulteration Act, 1954 is also illegal.
Section 16 (1) (a) (ii) refers to punishment for selling such food articles, which are adulterated.
In the present case, there is no report of any laboratory pointing out that food items sold by revisionist were adulterated.
It is thus urged that conviction awarded by the Court below is manifestly illegal and hence liable to be set aside by this Court.
Learned A.G.A. has contradicted the submissions urged by the learned counsel for the revisionist.
However, learned A.G.A. could not place before the Court the provisions or Rules under which licence is required for food items be sold by Revisionist who is a general merchant.

Learned A.G.A.
could not make such submissions on the basis of which submissions made by the learned counsel for the revisionist could be discarded.

In view of the above, this Court comes to the conclusion that in the absence of any finding recorded by the Court below that the revisionist was required to hold a licence in respect of Food items sold by him under any provision or Rules framed under Act, 1954, no offence can be said to have been committed by the revisionist under Section 7 (iii) of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

As there is no report saying that any items sold by the revisionist are adulterated, therefore, no offence under section 16 (1)(a)(ii) of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 can be said to have been committed by the revisionist.
For the reasons mentioned herein above, the present criminal revision succeeds and is allowed.

The order dated 13.2.2002 passed by the Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No. 2,
Allahabad and the order dated 8.7.2002 passed by Additional Sessions Judge, Court No. 12,
Allahabad are hereby set aside.
